items.title: Meta Open-Sources Muse Glimmer: A 30B Local Agentic Model Optimised for On-Device Execution
items.summary_1line: Meta AI Research has introduced Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model under the Apache 2.0 license, designed for local workflows. It enables autonomous agents and complex task execution on consumer GP...
items.editor_note: Names the model and confirms the Apache 2.0 license — the detail that makes it evaluable in production.

editorial.tldr: Meta entered the coding-agent market on Aug 9 with Muse Code, pitched directly against Claude Code and Codex. A day later a 30B Meta agent model appeared on Hugging Face at roughly 17GB, the first sign that Muse was a product family with a local tier rather than a single hosted agent.
editorial.whats_new: Meta open-sourced Muse Glimmer on Aug 14 — a 30B agentic model under Apache 2.0, sized to run autonomous agents and multi-step task execution on a consumer GPU.
editorial.why_it_matters: An Apache 2.0 30B agent model that fits in ~17GB is the first Muse tier you can run in your own VPC or on a workstation — the option that matters where hosted coding-agent spend or code-egress rules rule out Claude Code and Codex.
editorial.take_for_builders: Pull the weights and run your own tool-calling and SWE eval before treating Glimmer as a drop-in for a hosted coding agent — no independent benchmark against Claude Code or Codex has surfaced in this thread yet.

status.detail: Muse is now two tiers: a hosted coding agent (Muse Code) and an Apache 2.0 local model (Muse Glimmer), with no published head-to-head numbers for either.

beats.headline: Muse Glimmer lands under Apache 2.0 for local agent execution
beats.summary: Meta AI Research names the open-weight tier and licenses it permissively for autonomous agents on consumer GPUs.

open_questions: Is the ~17GB Hugging Face listing the same checkpoint as Muse Glimmer, or a separate quantized build?
How does Glimmer score on agentic tool-calling and SWE benchmarks against Claude Code and Codex?
What context window and tool-calling schema does Glimmer expose to existing agent harnesses?
Does Muse Code run on the Glimmer weights, or on a separate hosted-only model?
